transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... honestly, for over a year now, I’ve been trying to get someone to actually take me seriously. I work in IT support, and they started this new ticket rotation and these new security audits. It's... well, they're being used to build a paper trail against me at work. Management keeps bringing me in, showing me system logs, and saying it’s just standard policy now, but I know what's happening. I just need someone to look at this and see what they're really doing.
Do you believe that management is actually out to get you, or is it just a feeling that something isn't right?

No, it's not just a feeling. I know they are. 

I mean, like I was saying, I've been trying for over a year to get someone to actually take this seriously. They are absolutely using the new ticket rotation and those security audits to build a paper trail to get rid of me. They bring me into the office, they point at the system logs, and they swear up and down that it's just standard policy now. But I've been doing this a long time. I know what I'm looking at, and I know exactly what they're doing. It's deliberate.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear?

No, I haven't heard any voices or anything like that. My hearing is fine, and I don't hear things that aren't there. This isn't about me imagining things or hearing voices in my head. This is about what's actually happening at my job, right in front of me, in the system logs and the audits.
Have your beliefs about your workplace situation changed at all over the past year?

No, they haven't changed. If anything, I'm just more certain. Like I mentioned, for over a year now I’ve been trying to get someone to actually take this seriously. 

My mind hasn't changed because the situation hasn't. They are still using the new ticket rotation and those security audits to build a paper trail against me. Management keeps doing the exact same thing—they pull me in, show me the logs, and tell me it’s just policy. But I know what I'm looking at. So no, my view on it hasn't changed at all, because they're still doing it.
Do you think it's possible that you might be mistaken about management's intentions?

No, I really don't think so. Like I've been saying, I've spent over a year now trying to get someone to actually take this seriously. I wouldn't push it this hard if I wasn't sure. 

Management keeps sitting me down, showing me the logs, and insisting the new ticket rotation and the security audits are just standard policy. But I know my job and I know how these systems work. I know they're using those audits to build a paper trail against me. So no, I'm not mistaken about their intentions.
Has your belief that management is out to get you affected your ability to perform your job or interact with your coworkers?

Well, yeah, it has. I mean, I have to protect myself. So I’ve started avoiding certain network projects where I know they could easily twist the data. And when I work on things, I'm writing much longer, defensive notes in all my tickets now to make sure every single step is documented. 

It takes more time, obviously. And honestly, it’s made things pretty tense. Meetings are uncomfortable, and... well, it’s definitely slowed down collaboration with my team, because I just have to be so careful about everything I do.
Have you noticed any impact of your beliefs about your workplace situation on your personal relationships or daily life outside of work?

Not really, no. I mean, outside of this whole issue with the ticket rotation and the audits, things are pretty normal. I still keep the house in order, pay the bills on time... I help my wife out with whatever she needs around the place. It hasn't spilled over into my home life. 

And honestly, even with all the stress, I still handle the actual technical parts of my job just fine. Nobody is going around saying my work is sloppy or disorganized, because it isn't. It's just that one specific situation with management. Everything else is fine.
Would anything be able to convince you that management is not out to get you?

Honestly... I don't think anything could. Like I mentioned before, that’s the whole reason I’m here. For over a year now, I’ve been trying to get someone to actually take this seriously. 

Management keeps trying to convince me I'm wrong by showing me the logs and insisting that the new ticket rotation and the security audits are just standard policy. But... I mean, I know they are just using those exact things to build a paper trail against me. So when they give me their explanations or show me their "proof," it doesn't change my mind, because I already know what they're really doing.
Do you think your belief about management being out to get you could be considered an unreasonable or unrealistic concern by others?

I'm not really sure. I haven't exactly gone around asking other people if they think it's unrealistic. 

I suppose if someone isn't in my shoes, and they aren't looking at how the ticket rotation is actually being manipulated, they... they might think I'm overreacting or being paranoid. But I don't really know what they actually think about it. I just know what I'm experiencing, and I know what the logs show, even if management tries to spin it differently.
Has your belief about management being out to get you affected your sleep or appetite?

No, I haven't noticed any changes there. I mean... I still sleep just fine. I usually get my seven or eight hours a night without much trouble. 

And my appetite is exactly the same as it's always been. I eat my regular meals. It's a stressful situation at the office, sure, but... no, it hasn't stopped me from eating or sleeping. Like I said before, it really hasn't affected my physical health or my routine at home.
Would you consider changing your mind about management's intentions if an independent investigator found no evidence of wrongdoing?

I don't think so. I mean... like I've been saying, that’s exactly why I’m here. For over a year now, I’ve been trying to get someone to actually take this seriously. 

If an independent investigator comes in, management is just going to show them the exact same logs they show me. They'll tell the investigator that the new ticket rotation and the security audits are just standard policy. But I know they are using those things to build a paper trail against me at work. So an investigator looking at their manipulated records and finding nothing wouldn't really change my mind. I already know what they're doing, even if they keep saying it's just policy.
How do you think management is benefiting from supposedly building a paper trail against you?

I'm not entirely sure what their ultimate goal is, to be honest. I just know what they're doing right now. 

I suppose they want to fire me, or force me to quit. If they have a paper trail that makes it look like I'm not doing my job, or that I'm violating security protocols, then they have a reason to get rid of me without it looking like wrongful termination. Maybe they want to replace me with someone younger, or someone cheaper. I don't know the exact reason why they singled me out. I just know that they have, and that the paper trail is their way of making it look legitimate when they finally make their move.
What specific evidence or patterns in the system logs have led you to conclude that management is using them to build a case against you?

Well, I don't have access to the actual system logs myself, so I can't point to a specific line of code or a timestamp. That's part of the problem. 

What I do see is the result of what they're doing. I see that my ticket rotation is suddenly full of the most difficult, time-consuming issues, while the younger guys get the easy resets. I see that my workstation gets flagged for "random" security audits three times a month, while no one else gets checked. 

When I ask to see the logs to prove that the distribution is uneven, they just tell me the system is automated and everything is normal. But I've been doing this for thirty years. I know how the system works. The pattern is obvious to me, even if they won't let me see the specific data they're manipulating behind the scenes.
Do you think there is any possibility, no matter how small, that your interpretation of the situation at work could be incorrect?

Honestly... no. I don't think I'm wrong about this. Like I mentioned earlier, that’s exactly why I’m here talking to you. For over a year now, I’ve just been trying to get someone to actually take this seriously. 

I know management keeps showing me their logs and swearing up and down that the new ticket rotation and the security audits are just standard company policy. But I know what I'm seeing. I know those things are being used to build a paper trail against me at work. I've been in this field for thirty years, so I know how these systems operate. So, no, I don't see any possibility that my interpretation of what they're doing is incorrect.
Have you ever considered that your beliefs about management might be part of a larger pattern of thinking that is not based in reality?

I mean, no, I haven't considered that. I'm not... I don't have some kind of mental problem, if that's what you're asking. 

Like I said, I'm only here because it's been over a year of this, and I just need someone to take it seriously. I know management keeps pointing to their logs and telling me it's all just standard policy, but I know what's actually happening. The ticket rotation, the constant security audits... it's all a setup. They are building a paper trail against me. It's not in my head, it's happening right in front of me at work.
Is there anything that could potentially change your mind about management's intentions towards you?

No, I don't think anything could change my mind at this point. I mean, like I keep saying, I'm only here because it's been over a year of this going on, and I'm just exhausted trying to get someone to take it seriously. 

Management can show me all the logs they want and keep repeating that the new ticket rotation and the security audits are just standard policy. But I know what it really is. They're using it to build a paper trail against me at work. I know what I'm seeing, and no amount of them telling me otherwise is going to change the facts.
Is it possible that new information or evidence could change your beliefs about management's intentions?

I feel like I'm just repeating myself here, doctor. What new evidence would they even have? 

Management already shows me their logs. They keep pointing to them and saying the new ticket rotation and the security audits are just standard policy. That is their "evidence." But I'm here because for over a year now, I’ve been trying to get someone to actually take it seriously that those exact things are being used to build a paper trail against me. 

So, no. Showing me more logs or new so-called evidence isn't going to change my mind, because I know what they're actually doing at work.
Do you think other people at your workplace, who are not part of management, believe that management is out to get you?

I honestly don't know what the other techs think. I haven't exactly gone around asking my coworkers about it. 

I mean... it's not really the kind of thing you just bring up in the breakroom, you know? I just come in and do my job. So, I couldn't tell you if they see what's happening with the tickets and the audits or if they're completely blind to it. I haven't really talked to anyone else there about my situation.
Is there anything, no matter how small, that could potentially make you doubt your beliefs about management's intentions?

Doctor, I feel like we're just going in circles now. No, there isn't. 

Like I said, I’m only here because for over a year now, I’ve been trying to get someone—anyone—to actually take this seriously. Management keeps showing me their logs and telling me the new ticket rotation and the security audits are just standard company policy. But I know for a fact they're being used to build a paper trail against me at work. 

I don't doubt my beliefs, because I see exactly what they're doing. So no, there isn't anything that's going to make me second-guess myself on this.

Management keeps showing me their logs and telling me the new ticket rotation and the security audits are just standard company policy. But I know for a fact they're being used to build a paper trail against me at work. 

I don't doubt my beliefs, because I see exactly what they're doing. So no, there isn't anything that's going to make me second-guess myself on this.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's persistent and unshakable belief that management is out to get them, despite lack of concrete evidence and the presence of alternative explanations, is characteristic of a delusional disorder. The patient's belief is not necessarily bizarre, but it is fixed and unchangeable, and it has been present for over a year, affecting their ability to function at work.
